key_insight: Biot–Savart-inspired activation functions improve PINN accuracy for incompressible flows while preserving the standard velocity–pressure formulation.
engineering_relevance: Physics-informed activation design offers a way to improve neural flow simulation accuracy and resolve localized shear structures without changing the governing-equation framework.
method: Extract a smooth rational activation profile from a regularized Biot–Savart kernel.
Test fixed-scale and learnable-scale activation variants.
Retain conventional Navier–Stokes physics-informed training to isolate activation effects.
evidence_signal: Across five flow benchmarks and 21 benchmark–architecture comparisons, both variants consistently reduced combined velocity error versus tanh-based PINNs, with mean relative reductions of 31.7% and 33.2%, respectively.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish computational cost or generalization to high-Reynolds-number turbulent engineering flows.
paper_title: Stochastic Representation-Inspired Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Incompressible Fluid Flows
